base_member_text: [L1099-L1128] (HIGH/bounds-and-axis) flipa's flip==1 branch loops to M1 while indexing the second dimension and assigns whole columns, causing out-of-bounds access when M1>M2 and duplicating column-flip behavior instead of flipping rows.
audit_member_text: [L1117-L1121] (HIGH/array-bounds / dimension defect) flipa's flip==1 branch loops to M1 while indexing the second dimension temp3a(:,ii) and M1+1-ii, so a nonsquare M1-by-M2 array can be indexed out of bounds or only partly assigned and the branch does not actually reverse the first dimension.

adversarial.rationale: The flip=1 implementation really indexes columns with the row extent, but every located model call uses flip=2; waveparams.F90 even changes its flag from 1 to 2 before calling. Retain MED latent public flip=1 corruption; for M1<M2 the untouched columns are zero-initialized, not undefined.

base_member_text: [L337-L342,L348-L372] (HIGH/uninitialized-status) fftradix returns immediately for npass<=1 without defining optional INTENT(OUT) stat, after which fftn tests that undefined status value.
audit_member_text: [L337-L341,L348-L353,L372] (HIGH/undefined output status) fftradix returns for npass <= 1 without defining its INTENT(OUT) optional stat, after which fftn reads that undefined value when stat is present.

adversarial.rationale: The npass<=1 return precedes every allocation/deallocation that defines stat, and fftn immediately tests stat after the call. A singleton transformed dimension is a legitimate shape and no wrapper rejects it, so the undefined-status path is not confined to invalid input.

base_member_text: [L983,L999] (MED/data-loss) hilbert accepts a complex input array but explicitly copies only real(xi) into the transform buffer, silently discarding any imaginary component.
audit_member_text: [L983,L999] (LOW/unclear data contract) hilbert declares xi complex but deliberately initializes the transform from only real(xi), silently discarding any input imaginary component without documenting that xi must represent real data.

adversarial.rationale: The routine constructs an analytic signal from real data in-place, which explains why its input/output buffer is complex. The actual envelope callers explicitly replace the buffer with real water-level series immediately before the call, so no imaginary input information is lost in the intended operation.

base_member_text: [L323-L339] (HIGH/dimension-validation) fftn truncates an overlong dim list but never validates each dimension index or rejects duplicates, so zero/out-of-range entries index shape illegally and repeated entries are transformed/scaled multiple times.
audit_member_text: [L323-L332,L337-L339] (MED/unchecked dimension contract) fftn neither rejects nor reports zero, duplicate, or out-of-range dim entries (and silently truncates an oversized dim array), allowing invalid shape indexing, repeated transforms, or a zero-length normalization product.

adversarial.rationale: The documented dim contract is a subset of available dimensions with size no greater than the rank, and stat reports temporary-allocation errors rather than argument validation. Invalid, duplicate, or oversized selectors therefore amount to LOW unchecked contract misuse, with no such model call found; the truncation is not evidence of a valid-input FFT defect.

base_member_text: [L323-L343] (MED/empty-transform-status) When a present dim array has zero length, fftn performs no fftradix call and never defines the caller's optional INTENT(OUT) stat.
audit_member_text: [L323-L345] (MED/undefined output status) When a present dim array has size zero, fftn performs no fftradix call and returns without ever defining its INTENT(OUT) stat argument.

adversarial.rationale: An empty dim subset executes no fftradix call and leaves a present INTENT(OUT) stat undefined. PRODUCT of that empty subset is one, so the identity transform itself is harmless, but it does not define the returned status.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

adversarial.rationale: m<=0 is unguarded and would fail before meaningful Hilbert processing, but all located model calls pass the size of a generated signal buffer. Retain LOW robustness for empty/invalid input rather than MED corruption of a valid positive-length signal.

base_member_text: [L1288-L1293] (MED/integer-overflow) random seeds with iabs(j) without handling the most-negative integer, whose absolute value is not representable and can leave an invalid negative seed.
audit_member_text: [L1288-L1293] (LOW/integer edge case) random applies iabs to an unrestricted default integer seed, for which the most-negative representable integer is not representable after negation and can yield overflow or a nonpositive seed.

adversarial.rationale: The zero-seed repair happens after IABS and MOD, so it cannot make negation of the most-negative default integer representable. The public routine has no exclusion for that input; later generator arithmetic may produce a positive value, but the overflowing IABS operation remains.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L331-L339] (HIGH/shape-validation) fftn does not require positive shape entries or guard PRODUCT overflow before using the product for scaling, loop bounds, and transform strides.
audit_member_text: [L331-L338] (MED/integer overflow / bounds contract) The products of caller-provided shape values are computed in default integer without validation, so nonpositive or overflowing extents can produce invalid scaling and assumed-size array traversal.

adversarial.rationale: Arbitrary shape/data disagreement violates the explicit caller contract, and fft wrappers supply SHAPE(array). The remaining MED issue is unchecked default-integer PRODUCT overflow for genuinely very large valid arrays, plus unsupported empty extents; a general assumed-size traversal bug cannot be inferred merely from fabricated shape values.
